name: Act of July 13, 1892 providing, with the Coeur d'Alene's consent, for a 320-acre townsite tract at the mouth of the Coeur d'Alene River
aka: Indian appropriation act of 1892, Coeur d'Alene townsite provision
promises: The Act provided that, upon the consent of the Coeur d'Alene Indians obtained to the Secretary of the Interior's satisfaction, a tract of about 320 acres on the east shore of Coeur d'Alene Lake at the river mouth would be restored to the public domain on payment of five dollars an acre, the money to go to the Indians or be spent for their benefit.
landTaken: None found under this Act; the tract lies within the larger strip the tribe ceded by the agreement of February 7, 1894 (see cession-1894-08-15-coeur-d-al-ne).
compensation: The Act set five dollars an acre for the tract, payable to the tribe.
today: The Supreme Court in Idaho v. United States (2001) describes the later 1894 Harrison townsite cession (cession-1894-08-15-coeur-d-al-ne) as compensated to the Tribe and no one else.

sources.title: Charles C. Royce, Indian Land Cessions in the United States (18th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, 1899), schedule pp. 944-945
Act of July 13, 1892, ch. 164, 27 Stat. 120 (Indian appropriations, fiscal 1893)
Idaho v. United States, 533 U.S. 262 (2001)
sources.publisher: Caselaw Access Project, Harvard Law School Library

openQuestions: Whether the tribe gave the consent this Act required, or whether the 1894 agreement replaced it, was not found.
Indian Claims Commission Docket 81 concerns the Coeur d'Alene's aboriginal lands, not this tract.
The Coeur d'Alene Tribe's own account of the Harrison townsite was not located.

Audit 2026-11-08 (round 14): 'today' no longer says the 1894 cession 'succeeded this provision'; Idaho v. United States does not mention the 1892 Act. That the 1892 tract (half a mile south of the north line at the river mouth) lies inside the 1894 one-mile strip is the researcher's reading of the two descriptions (27 Stat. 120 and 28 Stat. 322), not a source's statement. The Act also let settlers already on the tract buy their lots at $5 an acre. Court of Claims case list (all 231 volumes) has no Coeur d'Alene case; ICC full-text 'Coeur Harrison' returns nothing.
